classes.name: Battery
classes.description: Chemical energy storage devices including Lithium-ion, Nickel-Cadmium, Lead-acid, and Alkaline batteries.
recycling_steps: Do NOT puncture, crush, or expose battery to open flame.
Tape both positive and negative terminals with non-conductive tape (electrical/duct tape) to prevent short circuits.
Store in a cool, dry, fire-safe container away from combustible materials.
Deliver to a specialized battery recycling bin, retailer drop-off kiosk, or municipal hazardous waste facility.
classes.reuse_potential: Secondary grid energy storage (for EV/Li-ion modules) or raw metal smelting

classes.name: Cable & Wires
classes.description: Power cables, USB cords, Ethernet cables, audio jacks, and internal ribbon wiring with high-grade metal cores.
recycling_steps: Separate damaged cables from reusable functioning cords.
Do NOT burn cables to extract copper (releases toxic dioxins and hydrochloric fumes).
Coil neatly and bundle with twist ties.
Deliver to specialized e-waste scrap centers equipped with mechanical cable granulators/strippers.
classes.reuse_potential: Direct reuse if functional, or granulated into pure copper pellets for remanufacturing

classes.name: Circuit Board / PCB
classes.description: Printed Circuit Boards (PCBs), motherboards, graphics cards, RAM sticks, and microcontroller boards rich in precious metals.
recycling_steps: Carefully unscrew and remove any coin-cell batteries (CR2032) or large aluminum heatsinks.
Handle board by the edges with gloves to avoid static discharge and contact with metal oxides.
Store in anti-static or cardboard packaging.
Hand over to certified R2 / e-Stewards recyclers utilizing hydrometallurgical or pyrometallurgical refining.
classes.reuse_potential: Component-level desoldering for repair parts, or precious metal hydrometallurgical smelting

classes.name: Mobile Phone & Tablet
classes.description: Smartphones, feature phones, and tablets with integrated displays, batteries, cameras, and processors.
hazardous_substances: Trace Arsenic in GaAs radio chips
recycling_steps: Perform a full factory data reset and remove iCloud / Google accounts to secure personal data.
Remove SIM card, MicroSD memory cards, and protective phone cases.
Inspect battery for swelling; if swollen, store in a fire-proof sand container immediately.
Deliver to mobile carrier buyback programs, manufacturer trade-in (Apple/Samsung), or certified e-waste recyclers.
classes.reuse_potential: Refurbishment, trade-in donation, or closed-loop precious metal reclamation

classes.name: Laptop & Computer
classes.description: Laptops, desktops, workstations, servers, and mini-PCs containing modular processing components.
hazardous_substances: Mercury vapor in older CCFL backlights
recycling_steps: Back up important files and securely wipe (DoD 5220.22-M) or physically remove storage drives (HDD/SSD).
Detach power adapter, external mice, and separate laptop battery if removable.
Disassemble modular parts (RAM, WiFi card, SSD) for reuse in other systems.
Deliver complete unit to electronics trade-in or certified computing recycling centers.
classes.reuse_potential: Hardware upgrade (SSD/RAM upgrade for Linux lightweight distro) or enterprise component harvesting

classes.name: Keyboard & Mouse
classes.description: Mechanical and membrane keyboards, optical and laser computer mice, and trackpads.
recycling_steps: Remove alkaline batteries from wireless models.
Disassemble keycaps and plastic shells for thermoplastic sorting and washing.
Separate metal springs and internal screws using magnets.
Submit plastics to municipal polymer recycling and internal circuits to e-waste bins.
classes.reuse_potential: Key switch lubing/repair, maker DIY keyboard mods, or pelletized plastic remolding

classes.name: Monitor & Display
classes.description: Computer monitors, LCD/LED screens, OLED panels, and legacy Cathode Ray Tube (CRT) monitors.
recyclable_materials: Power supply transformers and high-voltage capacitors
hazardous_substances: Mercury vapor inside CCFL cold-cathode fluorescent lamps
Lead oxide (up to 2-3 kg in CRT funnel glass)
recycling_steps: NEVER break, smash, or open the display glass—toxic mercury vapor and hazardous lead glass shards will escape.
Keep the panel intact and wrap screen surface in bubble wrap or cardboard for transit.
Detach power cable and stand for separate metal recycling.
Take directly to a designated hazardous electronic waste facility with specialized CRT/LCD dismantling robots.
classes.reuse_potential: Screen refurbishing, glass cullet for industrial sandblasting, or indium extraction

classes.name: Charger & Power Adapter
classes.description: Wall chargers, fast-charging bricks, laptop power bricks, and switching power supply adapters.
recycling_steps: Inspect if working; common 5V/12V adapters can be repurposed for DIY electronics and Arduino/Raspberry Pi projects.
Bundle DC cable with the brick to keep cords organized.
Do NOT attempt to crack open sealed high-voltage capacitors if recently plugged in.
Drop into small electronics recycling collection boxes at tech stores or municipal hubs.
classes.reuse_potential: Universal USB-C / DC power supply repurposing or copper transformer remelting

classes.name: Headphones & Audio Gear
classes.description: Over-ear headphones, in-ear earphones, Bluetooth earbuds, microphones, and portable speaker drivers.
recyclable_materials: Miniature Li-Po battery cells (in TWS earbuds)
hazardous_substances: Lithium coin cells (in true-wireless earbuds like AirPods)
recycling_steps: Detach silicone or foam ear cushions for general plastic/rubber recycling.
If wireless, ensure the charging case and earbuds are recycled together to safely process the miniature Li-ion cells.
Untangle and wrap audio cord neatly.
Deposit at audio brand trade-in drop boxes (e.g. Sony, Sennheiser, Apple) or electronics recyclers.
classes.reuse_potential: Driver/diaphragm replacement, neodymium magnet harvesting, or cable repurposing

classes.name: Storage Devices (HDD / SSD / CD)
classes.description: Magnetic Hard Disk Drives (HDD), Solid State Drives (SSD), USB Flash Drives, Optical CDs/DVDs, and SD cards.
hazardous_substances: Nickel alloy coating on magnetic platters
recycling_steps: CRITICAL: Wipe data with certified multipass overwrite tool (DBAN / BleachBit) or physically drill holes through HDD platters if discarding confidential data.
Remove aluminum top plate to harvest extremely strong neodymium actuator magnets for workshop use.
Separate solid-state PCB from aluminum SATA casing.
Deliver shredded or whole media to secure electronic waste destruction facilities.
classes.reuse_potential: Data wiping for secondary storage drive reuse, or aluminum alloy recycling
